subproblem.title: Coset averaging factors the index action on equivariant Hom complexes
subproblem.statement: Let k be a commutative ring, G a group with a Fintype structure, H a subgroup with a Fintype structure, A a k-linear G-representation, and X any chain complex of k-linear G-representations indexed by the natural numbers. The representations A and the terms of X lie in the same representation universe. Form the cochain complexes U = Hom_G(X,A) and V = Hom_H(Res_H X,Res_H A), with differential given by precomposition with the differential of X. There exist k-linear cochain maps R : U → V and C : V → U such that C ∘ R = [G:H] • id_U, where • denotes repeated addition of cochain maps. Neither normality of H nor finiteness or projectivity of A or the terms of X is assumed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {k G : Type _} [CommRing k] [Group G] [Fintype G] (A : Rep k G) (H : Subgroup G) [Fintype H] (X : ChainComplex (Rep k G) ℕ), ∃ R : Quiver.Hom (X.linearYonedaObj k A) (ChainComplex.linearYonedaObj (((Rep.resFunctor H.subtype).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj X) k (Rep.res H.subtype A)), ∃ C : Quiver.Hom (ChainComplex.linearYonedaObj (((Rep.resFunctor H.subtype).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj X) k (Rep.res H.subtype A)) (X.linearYonedaObj k A), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp R C = H.index • CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id (X.linearYonedaObj k A)
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Fix the stated data. Write U^m = Hom_G(X_m,A) and V^m = Hom_H(Res_H X_m,Res_H A). These are k-modules, and their differentials send F to F ∘ ∂_(m+1). They are exactly the two linearYonedaObj complexes in the statement. Let d = H.index.
2. Choose a left transversal T, one representative t for each left coset tH. Since G is finite, T is finite. The assignment t ↦ tH is a bijection from T to G/H, so |T| = d by the definition of subgroup index as the cardinality of G/H.
3. Define R_m : U^m → V^m by retaining the same underlying k-linear map and forgetting part of its equivariance. For F ∈ V^m define (C_m F)(x) = Σ_{t∈T} ρ_A(t)(F(ρ_(X_m)(t⁻¹)(x))). Each summand is k-linear in x, because all three maps being composed are k-linear. The expression is also k-linear in F, since composition with fixed linear maps and finite summation preserve addition and scalar multiplication.
4. For t ∈ G and h ∈ H, the summand indexed by th equals that indexed by t. Indeed, ρ_A(th)F(ρ_(X_m)((th)⁻¹)x) = ρ_A(t)ρ_A(h)F(ρ_(X_m)(h⁻¹)ρ_(X_m)(t⁻¹)x) = ρ_A(t)F(ρ_(X_m)(t⁻¹)x), using H-equivariance of F and cancellation of the actions of h and h⁻¹. Any two representatives of the same left coset differ by right multiplication by an element of H. Matching representatives by their cosets therefore proves that the finite sum defining C_m is independent of the chosen transversal.
5. Fix g ∈ G. Left multiplication permutes left cosets, and gT is another left transversal. Evaluate C_m F at ρ_(X_m)(g)x using gT. The summand indexed by gt is ρ_A(gt)F(ρ_(X_m)((gt)⁻¹)ρ_(X_m)(g)x) = ρ_A(g)ρ_A(t)F(ρ_(X_m)(t⁻¹)x). Summing and using linearity of ρ_A(g) gives (C_m F)(ρ_(X_m)(g)x) = ρ_A(g)((C_m F)(x)). Hence C_m F is G-equivariant. Together with step 3, this proves that C_m is a well-defined k-linear map V^m → U^m; R_m is k-linear as well.
6. Every differential ∂_(m+1) of X is G-equivariant. Thus ρ_(X_m)(t⁻¹) ∘ ∂_(m+1) = ∂_(m+1) ∘ ρ_(X_(m+1))(t⁻¹). Substituting this into the defining finite sum gives (C_m F) ∘ ∂_(m+1) = C_(m+1)(F ∘ ∂_(m+1)). Restriction plainly satisfies the same differential compatibility because it retains the underlying map. These identities, and the automatic identities for zero differentials outside adjacent degrees, assemble the R_m and C_m into cochain maps R and C.
7. If F ∈ U^m, its G-equivariance gives F(ρ_(X_m)(t⁻¹)x) = ρ_A(t⁻¹)F(x). Consequently every summand of C_m(R_m F)(x) is ρ_A(t)ρ_A(t⁻¹)F(x) = F(x). There are exactly d summands, so C_m(R_m F)(x) = d • F(x), with • denoting repeated addition.
8. Equality for every x proves C_m(R_m F) = d • F as equivariant linear maps. Equality for every F proves C_m ∘ R_m = d • id_(U^m). Natural-number multiplication on cochain morphisms is degreewise repeated addition, so equality in every degree proves C ∘ R = d • id_U. The maps from step 6 are the required witnesses.
proof_key_steps: Identify both cochain complexes as equivariant Hom modules with precomposition differentials.
Choose a finite left transversal and identify its cardinality with the subgroup index.
Define restriction and coset averaging, checking linearity.
Prove representative independence and use the translated transversal to establish G-equivariance.
Use equivariance of the chain differential to obtain cochain maps.
Evaluate averaging on G-equivariant maps and conclude the degreewise index identity.

The proof establishes transversal cardinality, representative independence, linearity, G-equivariance, differential compatibility, and the index identity without normality or projectivity assumptions. Its universe generality matches the prose. It neither relies on the parent nor on the other child; empty dependencies are correct and acyclic. The bare identifier is unreserved, and the frozen type contains no implementation-dependent reference.

subproblem.title: Restriction of the standard resolution is homotopy equivalent to the subgroup standard resolution
subproblem.statement: Let k be a commutative ring and G a group, both in one universe, and let H be any subgroup of G. Write B(L) = Rep.standardComplex k L: its degree-m term is the free k-module on L^(m+1), with diagonal left L-action and alternating vertex-deletion differential. There exists an H-equivariant chain homotopy equivalence between B(G) restricted to H and B(H). No finiteness or normality assumption is required.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {k G : Type _} [CommRing k] [Group G] (H : Subgroup G), Nonempty (HomotopyEquiv (((Rep.resFunctor H.subtype).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj (Rep.standardComplex k G)) (Rep.standardComplex k H))
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Fix k, G, and H. For L = G or H, write [g₀,…,g_m] for a free basis element of B(L)_m. The pinned standard-complex differential in positive degree is ∂_m[g₀,…,g_m] = Σ_{a=0}^m (−1)^a[g₀,…,ĝ_a,…,g_m]. There is no outgoing differential in degree zero. Restriction changes only the acting group, not these modules or differentials.
2. Choose one representative s of every right coset Hs, choosing 1 for H itself. Every g ∈ G has a unique expression g = hs with h ∈ H and s chosen: existence follows from membership in Hs; equality of two expressions first identifies the right coset and its chosen representative, and then right cancellation identifies h. Define r(g) = h and let i : H → G be inclusion.
3. If g = as and h ∈ H, then hg = (ha)s. Uniqueness gives r(hg) = h r(g). The representative of H is 1, so r(i(h)) = h. Thus r and i are H-equivariant maps of sets, and r ∘ i is the identity.
4. Apply r and i to every coordinate and extend k-linearly. This gives maps p_m : Res_H B(G)_m → B(H)_m and q_m : B(H)_m → Res_H B(G)_m. Their H-equivariance follows from step 3. Coordinatewise application commutes with every vertex deletion, hence with each alternating differential; the zero differentials also commute. Therefore p and q are chain maps, and p ∘ q is exactly the identity of B(H).
5. Put u(g) = g and v(g) = i(r(g)). These are H-equivariant. Define an H-equivariant k-linear map D_m : Res_H B(G)_m → Res_H B(G)_(m+1) by D_m[g₀,…,g_m] = Σ_{j=0}^m (−1)^j[ug₀,…,ug_j,vg_j,…,vg_m]. Every summand is H-equivariant because u and v are, so their signed sum is H-equivariant.
6. For m ≥ 1, expand ∂_(m+1)D_m + D_(m−1)∂_m on a basis tuple. In prism summand j, deletion of position a < j has sign (−1)^(j+a). It yields the same tuple as first deleting original vertex a and then using prism position j−1, whose sign is (−1)^(a+j−1); these cancel. Deletion of position a > j+1 has sign (−1)^(j+a). It yields the same tuple as first deleting original vertex a−1 and then using prism position j, whose sign is (−1)^(a−1+j); these also cancel. Every term of D_(m−1)∂_m is accounted for: for original deleted position b and subsequent prism position c, use the first pairing with j=c+1 and a=b when b≤c, and the second with j=c and a=b+1 when b>c.
7. The remaining deletions in prism summand j are positions j and j+1. Their contributions are respectively +[ug₀,…,ug_(j−1),vg_j,…,vg_m] and −[ug₀,…,ug_j,vg_(j+1),…,vg_m]. Summing over j cancels consecutive terms and leaves [vg₀,…,vg_m] − [ug₀,…,ug_m]. Thus ∂D + D∂ = v_* − u_* in positive degrees. In degree zero, D₀[g] = [ug,vg], whose boundary is [vg]−[ug]; this proves the same identity without any negative-degree term.
8. Since v_* = q ∘ p and u_* is the identity, D is a chain homotopy from q ∘ p to the identity of Res_H B(G). The equality p ∘ q = id from step 4 supplies the zero homotopy for the other composite. Taking p as the forward map and q as its homotopy inverse gives the required HomotopyEquiv and hence its Nonempty assertion.
proof_key_steps: Identify the pinned standard complex with free homogeneous tuples and alternating deletion.
Choose right-coset representatives with representative 1 for H and construct an H-equivariant retraction r : G → H.
Extend coordinatewise retraction and inclusion to chain maps with one composite exactly the identity.
Construct the H-equivariant prism operator between id_G and inclusion composed with r.
Pair all off-seam terms with opposite signs and telescope the seam terms, checking degree zero separately.
Package the two chain maps and their homotopies as a homotopy equivalence.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly expresses the stated homotopy equivalence, including the common universe and absence of finiteness assumptions. The normalized right transversal gives the claimed equivariant retraction. Coordinatewise maps commute with deletion. The two cancellation pairings exhaust the off-seam terms, the seam terms telescope to qp−id, and degree zero is checked explicitly. This matches Lean's Homotopy convention and supplies both required composite homotopies. The proof is complete and non-circular. The bare identifier is unreserved, and no child dependency is needed.
